title: Graham Capital Management's Tropin on Why Macro is Killing It

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Graham Capital Management's Tropin on Why Macro is Killing It.docx
meta.transcript source: YouTube auto-captions (no punctuation on this video's captions)

speakers: interviewer (Bloomberg Live host, name not given)
summary: Bloomberg Live interview (Oct 2022) with the founder of Graham Capital, a discretionary plus quant macro fund. Argues macro is thriving because central banks are moving rates sharply and diverging. Expects sticky inflation to 2025, long bonds mispriced, gold failed as hedge.

coverage.note: macro opportunity from central bank activity, divergence, BoJ, why 80s-90s were rich
macro unpopularity post-GFC, diversification, inflation stickiness, Fed easing timing
credibility camp, wage dynamics, European inflation, BoJ catalyst
equity range, term premium/long bonds mispriced, liquidity discipline, 2022 FX trades
fixed income shorts, crowded dollar, discretionary vs quant horizons, energy, crypto, gold

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - first reader caught all main views and methods; missed the 2022 return data point, the Fed over-tightening counter-view, front-end pricing path, real-rate view and the sterling neutral call

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: what drives macro performance and opportunities it's how much Central Bank movement there is
claims.claim: Macro opportunity set scales with the amount of central bank rate movement, because moves in policy rates drive FX and equity volatility.
claims.direction: more central bank movement = more FX/equity volatility = better macro opportunity
claims.testable: partly - could proxy opportunity by count of policy changes versus macro fund returns

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: in that 11-year period there were a total of 13 25 basis point equivalent hikes among all three
claims.claim: Data point: 2010-2021 saw only 13 25bp-equivalent hikes across ECB, BoE and Fed, versus 26 in 2022 alone with 44 priced for the year, explaining why macro was starved in the prior decade and rich now.
claims.testable: yes - count is checkable from policy rate histories

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: you have a very Divergent set of circumstances in Europe compared to the US compared to Japan and so on and so that's just good for macro Trading
claims.claim: Divergence in central bank policy across regions (Europe, US, Japan) creates relative-value and FX trades that favour macro trading.
claims.indicator: policy-rate divergence across major central banks
claims.direction: long dollar vs yen while BoJ holds its band
claims.testable: partly - divergence measure definable, link to returns needs testing

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the dollar ends at 146 or something today uh you know if they were to release that band there'd be a lot of opportunity on the downside in dollar Yen
claims.claim: If the Bank of Japan loosens its yield-curve band while dollar-yen is stretched near 146, there is large downside risk in USDJPY (a policy-change catalyst), whereas long dollar has paid so far.
claims.indicator: BoJ yield band (0.25% upper); USDJPY level
claims.direction: short USDJPY on band release; long USD until then
claims.conditions: depends on BoJ abandoning the band

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: markets were less efficient then and so when markets are inefficient there's a lot more to do and there tend to be overshoots and different uh you know uh Market momentum events
claims.claim: Macro was better in the 80s and 90s because markets were less efficient, producing more overshoots and momentum events; the efficient low-inflation 2010s left little to harvest.
claims.conditions: low-inflation, efficient-market regimes reduce macro opportunity

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: macro became an unpopular strategy it wasn't doing particularly well on the whole in that sort of post-gfc decade
claims.claim: Macro hedge funds were unpopular and weak post-GFC because inflation near zero and policy on hold made beta-heavy portfolios win.
claims.conditions: zero inflation and on-hold central banks hurt macro
claims.testable: partly - fund index returns by regime

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we generally generated positive returns so it didn't cost you money to be more Diversified and when you need that diversity in a year like this we're providing it
claims.claim: Macro funds delivered positive returns even in the weak decade and diversification when needed in 2022, so allocating to them was not costly.
claims.indicator: macro fund return correlation to equities/bonds

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: if you go back to the volkier it was really really tricky to get rid of inflation it took a very very long time it did not happen in two years
claims.claim: Volcker-era analogy: disinflation took far longer than two years and the central bank eased too early and had to hike again, so inflation is sticky and hard for the Fed to manage.
claims.direction: inflation stays above target for years; bonds unattractive

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: some of them are out of their purview the supply chain disruption the FED really can't manage that right and so the FED really can't manage what energy prices are
claims.claim: Supply-chain and energy-price driven inflation is outside Fed control, so rate hikes cannot fully remove it.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think the Market's expecting the FED to be able to start easing at the end of 2023 I'm skeptical
claims.claim: View: market pricing of Fed easing by end-2023 is too early; inflation falls in 2023 but is not near 2% until 2025 if then.
claims.indicator: Fed funds futures vs realised inflation
claims.direction: fade pricing of cuts in 2023; stay short duration

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think we want to err on the side of getting it comfortably down to Target it's going to be uh painful from for the economy Powell's conceded that
claims.claim: Credibility camp view: the Fed must over-tighten to re-anchor expectations, implying a recession whose timing and length are the open questions.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: inflation Genie got out of the bag it's hard to put it back in it's kind of like an ocean liner it takes a while for it to turn around
claims.claim: Inflation has momentum: once expectations and wage dynamics shift, disinflation is slow.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: you've got uh inflation in the Netherlands I believe it's 15 uh you've got the cost of power in Europe
claims.claim: European inflation is very high and supply-side driven by power costs, while US inflation is partly supply and partly labour-driven, which widens central bank divergence.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there is a complacency that has developed in the workforce where the expectation about constantly higher compensation and so on and firms competing for precious few employees have been you know contributing to inflation
claims.claim: Wage-price pressure from tight labour markets and employee expectations that have never seen a recession keep US inflation elevated and will reverse only slowly.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: corrodis tournaments up I think in April of uh 23 so that's going to be an important uh Catalyst to watch do they loosen that band
claims.claim: BoJ governor transition in April 2023 is a catalyst for loosening yield curve control, triggering a yen reaction (intervention already signals discomfort with weakness).

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we may be in a trading range for equities for some number of years
claims.claim: After 12 years of straight-up equities a more normal two-way market and a multi-year trading range is expected.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think it will be hotter for a while uh I think that's a I I don't disagree with the goal of having two percent inflation
claims.claim: Inflation will run above the 2% target for a while despite the target being worthy.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: for all of the years I've been in finance most of them there were something called duration risk for being in longer dated bonds and that's completely missing at the moment
claims.claim: Term premium is missing in long bonds; with inflation lasting several years, 10-year yields at 3.95% are mispriced and should be 50-100bp higher, with the curve re-steepening.
claims.conditions: if inflation persists three to five years

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we want to be able to exit positions without a great deal of expense and that's a Paramount uh you know importance to me
claims.claim: Risk approach: trade mostly very liquid markets, with daily risk committee, so positions can be exited cheaply and early rather than late at greater expense.
claims.testable: partly - liquidity constraint testable in backtests

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: it's been a great year to trade foreign exchange you know there's been a huge move in dollar euro dollar euro was 120 now it's you know 97 or something
claims.claim: 2022 FX trends (EURUSD 1.20 to 0.97, USDJPY higher, sterling down) were the best macro trades, consistent with rate divergence.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: income we've done quite well uh you know being short bonds of various durations and various different uh geographies
claims.claim: Short bonds across durations and regions plus energy and long dollar were profitable in 2022, as rates rose with inflation.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the dollar has been at profitable trade it's a crowded trade too do you think it has more room to run yeah it's definitely expensive
claims.claim: Long dollar is crowded and expensive, so the manager keeps only light exposure and expects only a little more upside.
claims.testable: partly - positioning data (CFTC) could be tested

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: our quantitative systems are somewhat longer term in nature they would tend to move around say over a period of weeks and months whereas our discretionary Traders they move very quickly
claims.claim: Two-layer structure: quant systems hold positions weeks to months while discretionary traders flip within days, staying open-minded to price information.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: one of the reasons I'm concerned about inflation being around for uh you know a longer period Than People expect is our energy policies are green
claims.claim: Underinvestment in conventional energy during the green transition plus OPEC supply cuts keeps energy (crude in the 90s) and headline inflation high, especially in Europe.
claims.indicator: crude oil price; energy supply policy

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we try and stay away from things that we really don't have an engine for
claims.claim: Discipline: keep crypto positions very small and avoid markets where the firm has no edge or process.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: if there was ever a year people wanted gold to perform and uh you know be an inflation hedge it's down
claims.claim: Gold failed as an inflation hedge in 2022, falling 10-15% while inflation spiked; speaker does not know why, but quant models were short.
claims.direction: gold did not hedge inflation; short gold

claims.speaker: interviewer
claims.quote: as I understand it your funds are up between 20 and 50 roughly and on the upper end again as many of you may know uh that's better than Bridgewater and it's better than Citadel
claims.claim: Data point: in the 2022 hiking year some macro managers were up 200% or more and Graham's funds roughly 20-50%, ahead of Bridgewater and Citadel, evidence that a regime of large central-bank moves pays macro strategies.
claims.indicator: macro hedge fund returns 2022 (Graham, Bridgewater, Citadel)
claims.direction: macro fund returns high in hiking years
claims.conditions: year of many large central-bank hikes (2022)
claims.testable: yes - macro/CTA index returns vs count of central-bank hikes by year

claims.speaker: interviewer
claims.quote: does Jay Powell's fed hike too much too fast and wreck the economy in the process because it has to regain the credibility that it lost calling inflation transitory
claims.claim: The opposing (Siegel) camp in the debate: a Fed trying to regain credibility lost by calling inflation transitory risks over-tightening too fast and causing avoidable economic damage (Tropin sides with the other camp).
claims.indicator: Fed hiking pace vs inflation expectations
claims.testable: partly - growth outcomes after fast hiking cycles

claims.speaker: interviewer
claims.quote: the other half at the very least of what you do and maybe it's more than half is trying to figure out how central banks will respond right to the data as they come out
claims.claim: Discretionary macro has two parts: forecasting the economic data and, at least as important, forecasting each central bank's reaction function to that data, which is where cross-country divergences come from.
claims.indicator: central-bank reaction function to data releases
claims.testable: partly - model policy-rate surprises conditional on data surprises

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the two-year is sort of pricing in 4-3 now for uh 75 at year end uh and then I think we start to see that ease back down in the middle of 23 to maybe four and a quarter
claims.claim: View (Oct 2022): the front end prices a policy peak near 4.75% by year-end easing to about 4.25% by mid-2023, while the 10-year sits at 3.95%, leaving the curve inverted; he sees the long end, not the front end, as mispriced.
claims.indicator: 2-year Treasury / priced policy path vs 10-year yield
claims.direction: front end peaks then eases; 10-year too low
claims.testable: yes - compare priced path with realised policy rates

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: Rachel rates have moved a lot but they needed to and I think they'll keep moving
claims.claim: Real rates have risen a lot, as was necessary, and will keep rising, which supports further bond weakness.
claims.testable: yes - subsequent change in TIPS real yields

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think it's already made a big move so I don't know how much weaker it really gets uh you know I so I would be kind of neutral at these levels personally
claims.claim: After sterling's large fall (bottom near 1.035), he is neutral: once a trend has already made a big move he sees little remaining edge in pressing it.
claims.testable: partly - returns after extreme multi-month currency moves
